title: Corvus lesson card file
description: One file per lesson. Card ids are permanent: review history is keyed by them.

language.description: BCP-47 code of the language being learned (e.g. 'la' for Latin).

parseCell.description: One cell of a grid: its row id and column id joined by '.', e.g. 'gen.sg'. Grids are defined in languages/<language>.json, and check-cards fails on a cell the grid doesn't have.

id.description: Permanent unique id: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens. Convention: <language>-<lesson as 2 digits>-<slug>.

lemma.description: The dictionary headword the card is about, spelled as the dictionary prints it, with its marks (e.g. 'aqua', 'amō' for amat). Compared after normalization, so case doesn't matter. Cards that share a lemma are siblings. It is also the answer of the reverse card.

prompt.description: What the learner sees. Markdown-lite: *italic* and **bold** only.

answer.description: The canonical answer. For parse cards, the list of every valid cell in the card's grid.

accept.description: Other answers that count as correct in typed modes. A reveal card shows them under the answer as 'also: ...'.

mode.description: Override the type's default answer mode.

grid.description: parse only: the id of a grid in languages/<language>.json. Without it, the language's defaultGrid is used.

reverse.description: vocab only: also generate a reverse card with id '<id>~r'. It shows this card's answer (and the hint) and expects the lemma, typed. Use true for a plain reverse card, or an object to add extras.

accept.description: Other target-language answers that count as correct.

hint.description: Shown with the prompt to rule out a near-synonym, e.g. 'not animus'.

retired.description: Hide the reverse card only; the forward card stays.

paradigm.description: ending only: the id of the paradigm in languages/<language>.json that the form belongs to. Requires cell.

cell.description: ending only: the form's cell in the paradigm's grid, e.g. 'gen.pl'. Requires paradigm.

strictMarks.description: Typed answers only: an answer that is right except for its marks is wrong, not a slip. For forms whose unmarked spelling is a different form the cards don't have yet (vēnit/venit).

notes.description: Shown after answering: pronunciation, chemistry links, usage.

speak.description: Text for the speak button if it differs from the target-language side.

retired.description: Hide from reviews without deleting history.
